written.q: Define a queue and state its access rule, operations and error conditions.
written.a: A queue is a linear data structure in which data additions are restricted to one end (rear) and removals can only be done from the other end (front). Access rule: First In First Out (FIFO). Operations: enqueue() and dequeue() (with create, destroy, isEmpty and, for the array version, isFull). Errors: overflow (adding to a full queue) and underflow (removing from an empty queue).

written.q: Why is the array-based queue made circular, and how is that done? Why is count needed?
written.a: Without wrapping, front and rear only move right and eventually run off the end of the array while cells at the left are free. Treating the array as a ring solves it: after enqueue rear ← rear MOD size, after dequeue front ← front MOD size, so an index reaching size returns to 0. When the queue is empty or full, front and rear are at the same place, so a count variable (0 or size) is needed to distinguish them.

written.q: Write the enqueue and dequeue algorithms of the array-based queue.
written.a:
ALGORITHM enqueue(VAL d DATATYPE)
1 IF (isFull())
2    RETURN false
3 ELSE
4    p[rear] ← d
5    rear ← rear + 1
6    count ← count + 1
7    rear ← rear MOD size
8    RETURN true
9 END IF
END enqueue

ALGORITHM dequeue(REF d DATATYPE)
1 IF (isEmpty())
2    RETURN false
3 ELSE
4    d ← p[front]
5    front ← front + 1
6    count ← count - 1
7    front ← front MOD size
8    RETURN true
9 END IF
END dequeue

written.q: Write the enqueue and dequeue algorithms of the linked list-based queue.
written.a:
ALGORITHM enqueue(VAL d DATATYPE)
1 p ← ALLOCATE MEMORY node
2 p->data ← d
3 p->next ← null
4 IF (front ≠ null)
5    rear->next ← p
6 ELSE
7    front ← p
8 END IF
9 rear ← p
END enqueue

ALGORITHM dequeue(REF d DATATYPE)
1 IF (isEmpty())
2    RETURN false
3 ELSE
4    d ← front->data
5    p ← front
6    IF (front = rear)
7       front ← rear ← null
8    ELSE
9       front ← front->next
10   END IF
11   RELEASE MEMORY p
12   RETURN true
13 END IF
END dequeue

written.q: An SMS gateway feeds incoming messages at one end of a data structure and releases them from the other in arrival order, for any number of messages. (a) Which data structure? (b) Illustrate it after MSG1, MSG2, MSG3 are fed in.
written.a: (a) A linked list-based queue (FIFO order, no fixed capacity). (b) front → [MSG1 | next] → [MSG2 | next] → [MSG3 | null] ← rear: three nodes linked in arrival order, front pointing at MSG1 and rear at MSG3.

written.q: Compare a stack and a queue, giving one application of each.
written.a: A stack is LIFO with additions and removals at one end (top), operations push and pop; a queue is FIFO with additions at the rear and removals at the front, operations enqueue and dequeue. Stack application: reversing data / undo / bracket matching. Queue application: printer spooling / process scheduling.
